input.content:
Patients don't judge a chiropractor by the adjustment table. They judge you by what they see first — your website, usually on a phone, usually while comparing you to two other practices in the same search results page. If the site looks dated, loads slowly, or doesn't clearly say where you are and how to book, they move on to the next listing. A good site isn't a nice-to-have for a chiropractic practice; it's the first impression that decides whether someone calls.

What chiropractors actually need from a website

Chiropractic patients are usually dealing with pain, and pain makes people impatient. Someone searching "chiropractor near me" at 11pm with a stiff back wants three things fast: proof you're legitimate, proof you're close by and open, and an obvious way to reach you. Everything else — your philosophy of care, your equipment, your Instagram feed — is secondary to those three jobs.

That means your site needs to be credible-looking on a phone screen in under three seconds, clear about your specialties (sports injuries, prenatal care, sciatica, general wellness — whatever you actually treat), and structured so Google and a rushed human can both find your address and hours without hunting.

The must-have sections

Every chiropractic site, regardless of how big the practice is, needs the same handful of sections done well. Skip one and you're leaving patients — and search ranking — on the table.

Services

List what you treat in plain language, not textbook terms. "Lower back pain," "sports injuries," "prenatal chiropractic," and "sciatica" get searched far more often than "subluxation correction." Give each service its own short block so both patients and Google can match a search to a specific page.

About

Patients are trusting you with their spine — they want to know who you are before they book. A short bio, your credentials, your years in practice, and a real photo do more for conversion than almost anything else on the site.

Location and hours

Your address, a map, parking notes if relevant, and hours need to be visible without a click. This is also one of the strongest local SEO signals you control directly on the page itself.

Appointment request

A clear, prominent way to request an appointment — name, phone, preferred day, and what's bothering them. Worth being upfront here: a Kodely-built site gives you a genuinely good-looking, working request form and a clear "Call Us" path, but it doesn't connect to a calendar or booking database on its own yet. You'll want to point the form's contact info at whatever scheduling tool or front-desk process you already use, or simply have staff follow up on submissions.

Patient reviews

Nothing sells "this chiropractor is legit" like a handful of real patient stories. Even three or four short testimonials, with a first name and what they came in for, meaningfully increase trust for someone who's never heard of your practice.

Example prompt: building a real chiropractic site

Here's exactly the kind of prompt that works well in Kodely's chat interface. Copy it, swap in your own details, and paste it in to start:

"Build a website for Northgate Chiropractic & Wellness, a chiropractic practice in Lakeview, IL run by Dr. Elena Marsh. We treat back pain, sports injuries, and offer prenatal chiropractic care. Include a home page with a warm welcome message and a clear 'Request an Appointment' button. Add a Services page listing Spinal Adjustments, Sports Injury Rehab, Prenatal Chiropractic, and Massage Therapy, each with a short description. Add an About page with Dr. Marsh's bio and credentials. Add a Location & Hours page with our address at 482 Elm Street, Lakeview, IL, and hours Monday to Friday 8am–6pm, Saturday 9am–1pm. Add a Patient Reviews section with 3–4 short testimonials. Use a calming, professional palette of soft blues and greens, clean sans-serif fonts, and make sure everything looks great on mobile."

Kodely reads that and generates a real Vite + React + TypeScript site — actual component files for each page, built from hand-crafted UI primitives, not a locked-down template. You'll see it compiling in a live preview as it's built, and you can keep refining it the same way: "make the hero photo bigger," "add a phone number to the header," "change the accent color to teal."

What you actually get

  • Real code, not a page builder. Every project is a genuine Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4 app, with its own component files from the first prompt.
  • A live preview that shows the actual compiled app as Kodely builds it, so you're never guessing what you'll get.
  • One-click publish to a free public URL at yourpractice.kodely.site — no separate hosting step, no credit card required to try it.
  • Chat-based editing. Describe a change in plain English and Kodely edits the real components behind the scenes. There's no drag-and-drop visual editor yet — it's conversational.
  • Free checkpoints. Every successful generation is a save point, so you can roll back to an earlier version at no cost if a change doesn't land the way you wanted.
  • Code view. You can see and copy the generated source directly in the app. There's no zip download or full project export yet, so plan to keep working inside Kodely for now.

Worth knowing before you start: sites currently publish to a *.kodely.site subdomain rather than a custom domain like yourpractice.com, and there's no built-in database or online booking system yet — the appointment form collects a request, but you'll route it to your own phone, email, or scheduling tool.

New accounts get 750 free credits, no card needed, and a typical first build for a site like this runs roughly 100–150 credits — enough to build and iterate on the whole thing a few times over. A build that fails to compile is never charged. If you need more, top-ups run from $9 for 500 credits up to $90 for 6,000 credits, and credits never expire. See pricing for the full breakdown.

Tips for local SEO once your site is live

  • Claim and complete your Google Business Profile with the exact same practice name, address, and phone number that appear on your site. Consistency between the two matters more than almost anything else for local rankings.
  • Use your city and neighborhood in your page text naturally — "chiropractor in Lakeview, IL" reads better and ranks better than a generic "Services" page with no location mentioned anywhere.
  • Ask happy patients for Google reviews and feature a few of the best ones on your site itself; review volume and recency are a real ranking factor for local search.
  • List your specialties as separate, specific phrases — "prenatal chiropractic," "sports injury rehab," "sciatica treatment" — rather than burying them all in one paragraph, since people search for the specific problem they have.
  • Keep your hours and contact info identical everywhere your practice is listed online — your site, your Google profile, and any directories — since mismatched hours are a common reason patients (and search engines) lose trust.

FAQ

Can Kodely build online booking for my practice?

Not yet. Kodely builds a genuinely good-looking appointment request page and contact form, but it doesn't save bookings to a calendar or database on its own. Most practices point the form at their existing front desk process or scheduling tool, or simply have staff call back on new requests.

Can I use my own domain, like northgatechiro.com?

Not yet — published sites currently live on a free *.kodely.site subdomain (for example, northgatechiro.kodely.site). Custom domain support isn't available today.

Do I need to know how to code?

No. You describe what you want in plain English in the chat, and Kodely writes and assembles the actual React components. If you do want to look under the hood, there's a code view where you can see and copy the generated source.

Can I download or export the code?

Not yet — there's no zip download or full project export at this stage. You can view and copy source from the in-app code view, but ongoing edits are made through Kodely's chat interface.

What does it cost to build a site like this?

New accounts start with 750 free credits and no card is required. A first build for a chiropractic site typically costs around 100–150 credits, which leaves plenty of room to try a few directions before you'd need to top up. Full details are on the pricing page.

What if I don't like a change I made?

Every successful generation creates a checkpoint automatically, and rolling back to a previous version is free. You can experiment with wording, colors, or layout changes without worrying about losing a version you liked better.

How do I get started?

Create a free account at /signup — no credit card needed — and describe your practice in the chat the same way the example prompt above does. If you already have an account, head to /login to jump back into your project. You can also browse the blog for more build examples, or head back to the homepage to see what else Kodely can build.

1 {"slug": "website-builder-for-chiropractors", "title": "AI Website Builder for Chiropractors: Launch in Minutes", "metaTitle": "AI Website Builder for Chiropractors: Launch in Minutes", "metaDescription": "Describe your chiropractic practice in a chat and Kodely builds a real, mobile-friendly site with services, hours, and reviews — publish free in minutes.", "targetKeyword": "website builder for chiropractors", "category": "Industries", "bodyHtml": "

Patients don't judge a chiropractor by the adjustment table. They judge you by what they see first — your website, usually on a phone, usually while comparing you to two other practices in the same search results page. If the site looks dated, loads slowly, or doesn't clearly say where you are and how to book, they move on to the next listing. A good site isn't a nice-to-have for a chiropractic practice; it's the first impression that decides whether someone calls.

What chiropractors actually need from a website

Chiropractic patients are usually dealing with pain, and pain makes people impatient. Someone searching "chiropractor near me" at 11pm with a stiff back wants three things fast: proof you're legitimate, proof you're close by and open, and an obvious way to reach you. Everything else — your philosophy of care, your equipment, your Instagram feed — is secondary to those three jobs.

That means your site needs to be credible-looking on a phone screen in under three seconds, clear about your specialties (sports injuries, prenatal care, sciatica, general wellness — whatever you actually treat), and structured so Google and a rushed human can both find your address and hours without hunting.

The must-have sections

Every chiropractic site, regardless of how big the practice is, needs the same handful of sections done well. Skip one and you're leaving patients — and search ranking — on the table.

Services

List what you treat in plain language, not textbook terms. "Lower back pain," "sports injuries," "prenatal chiropractic," and "sciatica" get searched far more often than "subluxation correction." Give each service its own short block so both patients and Google can match a search to a specific page.

About

Patients are trusting you with their spine — they want to know who you are before they book. A short bio, your credentials, your years in practice, and a real photo do more for conversion than almost anything else on the site.

Location and hours

Your address, a map, parking notes if relevant, and hours need to be visible without a click. This is also one of the strongest local SEO signals you control directly on the page itself.

Appointment request

A clear, prominent way to request an appointment — name, phone, preferred day, and what's bothering them. Worth being upfront here: a Kodely-built site gives you a genuinely good-looking, working request form and a clear "Call Us" path, but it doesn't connect to a calendar or booking database on its own yet. You'll want to point the form's contact info at whatever scheduling tool or front-desk process you already use, or simply have staff follow up on submissions.

Patient reviews

Nothing sells "this chiropractor is legit" like a handful of real patient stories. Even three or four short testimonials, with a first name and what they came in for, meaningfully increase trust for someone who's never heard of your practice.

Example prompt: building a real chiropractic site

Here's exactly the kind of prompt that works well in Kodely's chat interface. Copy it, swap in your own details, and paste it in to start:

"Build a website for Northgate Chiropractic & Wellness, a chiropractic practice in Lakeview, IL run by Dr. Elena Marsh. We treat back pain, sports injuries, and offer prenatal chiropractic care. Include a home page with a warm welcome message and a clear 'Request an Appointment' button. Add a Services page listing Spinal Adjustments, Sports Injury Rehab, Prenatal Chiropractic, and Massage Therapy, each with a short description. Add an About page with Dr. Marsh's bio and credentials. Add a Location & Hours page with our address at 482 Elm Street, Lakeview, IL, and hours Monday to Friday 8am–6pm, Saturday 9am–1pm. Add a Patient Reviews section with 3–4 short testimonials. Use a calming, professional palette of soft blues and greens, clean sans-serif fonts, and make sure everything looks great on mobile."

Kodely reads that and generates a real Vite + React + TypeScript site — actual component files for each page, built from hand-crafted UI primitives, not a locked-down template. You'll see it compiling in a live preview as it's built, and you can keep refining it the same way: "make the hero photo bigger," "add a phone number to the header," "change the accent color to teal."

What you actually get

  • Real code, not a page builder. Every project is a genuine Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4 app, with its own component files from the first prompt.
  • A live preview that shows the actual compiled app as Kodely builds it, so you're never guessing what you'll get.
  • One-click publish to a free public URL at yourpractice.kodely.site — no separate hosting step, no credit card required to try it.
  • Chat-based editing. Describe a change in plain English and Kodely edits the real components behind the scenes. There's no drag-and-drop visual editor yet — it's conversational.
  • Free checkpoints. Every successful generation is a save point, so you can roll back to an earlier version at no cost if a change doesn't land the way you wanted.
  • Code view. You can see and copy the generated source directly in the app. There's no zip download or full project export yet, so plan to keep working inside Kodely for now.

Worth knowing before you start: sites currently publish to a *.kodely.site subdomain rather than a custom domain like yourpractice.com, and there's no built-in database or online booking system yet — the appointment form collects a request, but you'll route it to your own phone, email, or scheduling tool.

New accounts get 750 free credits, no card needed, and a typical first build for a site like this runs roughly 100–150 credits — enough to build and iterate on the whole thing a few times over. A build that fails to compile is never charged. If you need more, top-ups run from $9 for 500 credits up to $90 for 6,000 credits, and credits never expire. See pricing for the full breakdown.

Tips for local SEO once your site is live

  • Claim and complete your Google Business Profile with the exact same practice name, address, and phone number that appear on your site. Consistency between the two matters more than almost anything else for local rankings.
  • Use your city and neighborhood in your page text naturally — "chiropractor in Lakeview, IL" reads better and ranks better than a generic "Services" page with no location mentioned anywhere.
  • Ask happy patients for Google reviews and feature a few of the best ones on your site itself; review volume and recency are a real ranking factor for local search.
  • List your specialties as separate, specific phrases — "prenatal chiropractic," "sports injury rehab," "sciatica treatment" — rather than burying them all in one paragraph, since people search for the specific problem they have.
  • Keep your hours and contact info identical everywhere your practice is listed online — your site, your Google profile, and any directories — since mismatched hours are a common reason patients (and search engines) lose trust.

FAQ

Can Kodely build online booking for my practice?

Not yet. Kodely builds a genuinely good-looking appointment request page and contact form, but it doesn't save bookings to a calendar or database on its own. Most practices point the form at their existing front desk process or scheduling tool, or simply have staff call back on new requests.

Can I use my own domain, like northgatechiro.com?

Not yet — published sites currently live on a free *.kodely.site subdomain (for example, northgatechiro.kodely.site). Custom domain support isn't available today.

Do I need to know how to code?

No. You describe what you want in plain English in the chat, and Kodely writes and assembles the actual React components. If you do want to look under the hood, there's a code view where you can see and copy the generated source.

Can I download or export the code?

Not yet — there's no zip download or full project export at this stage. You can view and copy source from the in-app code view, but ongoing edits are made through Kodely's chat interface.

What does it cost to build a site like this?

New accounts start with 750 free credits and no card is required. A first build for a chiropractic site typically costs around 100–150 credits, which leaves plenty of room to try a few directions before you'd need to top up. Full details are on the pricing page.

What if I don't like a change I made?

Every successful generation creates a checkpoint automatically, and rolling back to a previous version is free. You can experiment with wording, colors, or layout changes without worrying about losing a version you liked better.

How do I get started?

Create a free account at /signup — no credit card needed — and describe your practice in the chat the same way the example prompt above does. If you already have an account, head to /login to jump back into your project. You can also browse the blog for more build examples, or head back to the homepage to see what else Kodely can build.

"}
